definitions.gloss: covert operative; secret agent; undercover agent
definitions.explanation: A person sent by a state or organization to carry out clandestine activity — espionage, sabotage, or influence operations — in another country or group. Almost always used of the other side, never as a neutral job title.

examples.japanese: {工作員|こうさくいん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{潜入|せんにゅう}していた→潜入する：20994_sennyuusuru⟧。
examples.english: An operative had infiltrated the group.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{外国|がいこく}→外国：02868_gaikoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{工作員|こうさくいん}だ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{疑|うたが}われている→疑う：01889_utagau⟧。
examples.english: He is suspected of being a foreign agent.

examples.japanese: {工作員|こうさくいん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{偽|いつわ}り→偽り：09999_itsuwari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{情報|じょうほう}→情報：03348_jouhou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{流|なが}して→流す：01968_nagasu⟧⟦{世論|よろん}→世論：16145_yoron⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{動|うご}かそう→動かす：01885_ugokasu⟧としたらしい。
examples.english: Operatives apparently tried to sway public opinion by spreading false information.

notes:
Formed from ⟦{工作|こうさく}→工作：12437_kousaku⟧ (maneuvering, covert operations) plus the suffix {員|いん} (member, staff). Note that ⟦{工作|こうさく}→工作：12437_kousaku⟧ on its own also means "handicrafts" — the school subject — so the covert sense comes entirely from the compound and its context.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {工作員|こうさくいん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{送|おく}り⟦{込|こ}む→込む：00719_komu⟧: to send in an operative
- {工作員|こうさくいん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{潜入|せんにゅう}する→潜入する：20994_sennyuusuru⟧: for an operative to infiltrate
- ⟦{産業|さんぎょう}→産業：01419_sangyou⟧{工作員|こうさくいん}: industrial spy

REGISTER:
The word carries a strong negative charge and is common in news reports and thrillers. Online it is also thrown around loosely as an insult, accusing someone of posting on behalf of a foreign government.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦スパイ→スパイ：18236_supai⟧: spy — broader and more neutral; focuses on gathering information
- ⟦{諜報員|ちょうほういん}→諜報員：30160_chouhouin⟧: intelligence agent — formal, specifically about intelligence work
